exposure: internal manoeuvres (Woods' screw, reverse Woods' screw, removal of the posterior arm)
cohort: The study included 403 women who experienced shoulder dystocia at birth.
finding: Shoulder dystocia was associated with a three-fold increase in the risk of OASIS, with specific internal manoeuvres and a higher number of manoeuvres significantly increasing this likelihood.
mod_finding: Instrumental deliveries were independently associated with a higher incidence of OASIS.
